Choose the separating action before selecting an account: at tick 0 validate N3 and individually request N2. Predeclare the continuation: validate N4,N5,N6,N7,N8 at ticks 1,2,3,4,5; request individual N3 at 1 and N4 at 2; idle dispatcher at 3; bulk at 4; individual N7 at 5 and N8 at 6; then idle. Probe this exact finite trace through boundary 9 using registration, queue, recognition and dashboard ledgers. Bulk at 4 should select N5,N6 after N1 and prior deliveries clear.

Retain incompatible hypotheses until the separating trace is checked: clearance followed by batching can amortize requests enough to finish; alternatively, batching necessarily introduces another lost delivery slot or requires a seventh action. Closest operational rival is individual-only dispatch, which avoids duplicates but needs seven requests for seven remaining identities. Neither hypothesis earns selection from its name.

Defeat the impossibility account if the same trace records eight registrations and eight recognitions within budget. Preserve any queue mismatch rather than relabeling requests as success.
